tweets.text:
Inside Photon, p99 response time dropped from about 800 ms to about 65 ms. It uses about 20% fewer serving machines and stores 2.5x as much data per document.

How we built Photon: https://t.co/7c64kR5OB5
Get started with Fast Search: https://t.co/Qn4OPZfqnx

Photon builds new indexes separately from the servers handling live queries.

When a version is ready, Photon updates one serving group at a time, warms its caches with real search queries, checks readiness, and returns it to routing. The other groups keep serving traffic. https://t.co/QQGO7YbomE

Photon stores the index in compact formats, so each query reads and decodes only what it needs.

When data has to come from disk, Photon batches the reads and runs them asynchronously, so a query isn't stuck waiting on disk. https://t.co/YjGrF1CPzx

“Reinforcing Agents with Collective Skills”

Thousands of developers have published Agent Skills on GitHub that contains instruction files which teach agents how to perform specific workflows.

Skill2Env crawls these Skills and turns 3.4k of them into ~8k executable RL environments, preserving the workflows and quality criteria their authors wrote down.

And after just 300 RL steps, Qwen3.8-27B gains +4.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and +4.3 on S2EBench.

https://t.co/3yYjSZn8FQ

"HySparse2: Hybrid Sparse Attention with Two-Level KV Sharing"

Xiaomi dropped their new attention mechanism for their upcoming V3 model.

Their new HySparse2 makes long-context agents much cheaper by sharing KV caches across layers instead of repeatedly processing and storing the entire context.

With two-level KV sharing and token-level sparse attention, HySparse2 can stop prefill halfway through the model while still retrieving the right tokens from long contexts.

At 1M context, it cuts prefill FLOPs by 2.92x vs HySparse and shrinks the KV cache from 6.72GB to 2.69GB, improving long-context retrieval by a lot.

https://t.co/bZZq0qGs6M
